multiplechoiceresponse.p: A user reports a message demanding payment to unlock their files. Your first action should be to:

choice.div: Pay the demand to recover the files quickly.
Run a full antivirus scan and continue working.
Isolate the device from the network and report the incident immediately.

div.p: This is a likely ransomware event. Isolate the device to stop the spread and escalate through the security incident channel — do not attempt to clean it yourself.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which is the strongest phishing indicator?

choice.div: A message creating urgency to enter credentials at a slightly misspelled domain.
A message from a colleague with a normal signature.
A newsletter you subscribed to arriving on schedule.

div.p: Urgency plus a near-miss domain is the classic phishing pattern. Hover over links, verify the sender, and never enter credentials from an email link.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which form of multi-factor authentication is the most phishing-resistant?

choice.div: A one-time code sent by SMS
A code from an authenticator app typed into a website
A hardware security key (FIDO2) tied to the site's origin

div.p: FIDO2 hardware keys bind the credential to the real site origin, so a fake login page cannot relay it. SMS codes are the weakest and are vulnerable to interception.

choiceresponse.p: Which of the following are good password practices? Select all that apply.

choice.div: Use a long, unique passphrase for every account.
Store passwords in a password manager.
Reuse one strong password across all sites.
Share the password with IT so they can help you.

div.p: Length, uniqueness, and a password manager are the core practices. Reuse means one breach exposes every account, and support never needs a user's password.
